Try it on the continuous video.

Actual 90-second playback with estimates at 0.5-second intervals. The accepted per-frame ice geometry supplies each observation. Track IDs remain provisional and camera-local.

Proposals can still be equipment, parked stones or merged stones. The height correction does not fix those detection errors. No scoring or complete state is inferred.

TrackPositionSensitivity

Sensitivity varies height by ±2 cm, pixel aspect by ±10%, and principal point by ±5% of the panel size, one at a time. It is not a probability, confidence interval or complete error bound.

The architecture is now explicit.

1 · Body evidence

High-angle images: circular body-outline proposals, checked against expected size, a neutral rim and a coloured interior. Low-angle images: body-supported cap proposals. Detection runs on original source pixels.

2 · Camera and feature height

Infer a conditional pinhole camera from the ice homography. Back-project the feature at its assumed height instead of pretending it sits on the ice. Reject inconsistent low-angle pose estimates.

3 · Provisional ground position

Emit metric coordinates, the localization method, sensitivity diagnostics and image evidence. A near-overhead approximation is labelled explicitly when focal length is unidentifiable.

Method, assumptions and what still needs validation

This is a classical computer-vision baseline, not a trained neural detector. The new high-angle branch detects body outlines; the low-angle branch retains the previous cap proposal generator and adds conditional 3D correction. Stone radius is assumed to be 13.9 cm; cap-plane height is assumed to be 13.6 cm and body-centre height 6.8 cm. These feature heights are approximations, not measurements of the observed cap surfaces.

The camera assumes zero skew, square pixels and a principal point at the centre of the camera panel. Cropping, resizing, unknown lens distortion and occlusion can violate those assumptions. A homography alone does not establish a uniquely calibrated 3D camera.

Benchmark labels and reference links stay frozen, but this version was developed with those examples already known. The next accuracy claim needs an untouched recording and independently checked ground positions. The current video demonstration has no measured metric stone accuracy.
